newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia customs ban mostly spares air couriers.
newsitem.headline: Russia customs ban mostly spares air couriers.

text.p: New customs rules have not hurt air couriers operating in Russia as badly as expected, creating a more stable cargo market in April than the previous month, Western firms said on Monday.

Under a Russian customs rule imposed on March 20 shippers are barred from automatically forwarding cargo into the Russian provinces through Moscow. Rather clients must come personally to Moscow to clear customs.

"We had some troubles during first days after the ban was imposed, but the four leading courier firms were able to get permission from customs so that the law does not affect their activities," said Ivan Shatskikh, U.S. courier United Parcel Service's local financial director.
As a result, UPS saw a small increase in April volume compared with the previous month, and expected a very active market in May, Shatskikh said.
"The market has been growing during last few years. This is a very good trend," he said.
Igor Filatov, TNT's sales manager, said his company handled more export shipments last month compared with March. "But we had some difficulties with Russia's new customs laws," he said.
Filatov said that TNT's volumes were lower during first days of May due to the May Day holidays.
He added said that competition between four leading courier firms, operating in Russia -- TNT, UPS, DHL and FedEx -- became sharper.
"Nobody is sleeping in this market," he said. "We see it as very promising."
But for Federal Express the market was weaker in April compared with March, according to Ben Scott, marketing specialist for Central and Eastern Europe.
"I believe that the overall market must be soft in April, perhaps because shippers are nervous because things seem so unstable recently," he said.
Marina Petropalovskaya, DHL marketing manager, said April volumes were the same as in March.
"We hoped the competition would be very strong, but this forecast was wrong," she said.
Officials from the major air courriers said rates did not change over the past month.
The cost of sending a half-kilo parcel (one pound) from Moscow to North America, Canada or Mexico varied between $55 with FedEx and $61 with TNT.

A similiar package from Moscow to Western Europe cost between $50 for UPS and $58 for DHL, and between $65 for UPS and $75 for DHL from Moscow to South East Asia and Japan. --Viktor Anoshkin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
